props.backstory:
Backstory

Farin Fatuus was an orphan raised at a monastery in one of Sol’s farming villages. During childhood she discovered a secret gift: her eyes showed brief, razor-sharp visions of moments yet to come. She played orphanage games as if dancing to music only she could hear and quietly solved villagers’ troubles before they even formed—gaining praise that swelled her pride as bright as any star.

She kept the gift hidden, knowing how different it made her, until one fateful night when she chose to revealed her secret to a close friend. The girl, terrified of “demonic augury,” alerted the Church Inquisition. Thanks to her future-sight Farin narrowly escaped, but a stray chunk of debris from a magical blast struck her right eye, blinding it and taking half her gift. The applause she once basked in—when she “miraculously” solved harvest woes or never missed a marble shot—now rang hollow: the villagers had praised the gift, not the girl. This start her belief that the world is all a series of "right" or "wrong" choice, and entrusting her secrets to her close feidn was the "wrong" choice. With one eye shattered, the other became a lifeline to the superiority she could not bear to lose. Wounded and alone, she was rescued by Lyra, a master astrologian who had foreseen “a fallen comet child” in her charts. Under Lyra’s tutelage Farin learned the patient art of true astrology.

Time passed. One day Farin learned of a ritual said to let a seer glimpse her own destiny, and her ambition flared. She believed knowing her future would lead to everlasting happiness. When she asked, Lyra warned that peering into one’s own fate was folly: “If you already know what you want to do with life, certainty adds nothing.” Ignoring her teacher, Farin performed the rite during a lunar eclipse, using her remaining eye as the catalyst. The vision—a towering World Tree on the brink of ruin—shattered mid-revelation as a celestial force severed her foresight, branding her pupil with the Astral Severance curse. Sightless to tomorrow for the first time, she fled in anger, convinced that only by regaining absolute foresight could she secure true happiness.

Now sixteen, cloak drawn tight against storm-spray, Farin scours the seas for a rumored artifact said to lift any astral affliction. Companions may see a sharp-tongued seer stripped of certainty; she sees a single path: reclaim her prophetic gaze and prove that knowing every answer will, indeed, lead to everlasting joy—no matter what doom the stars once showed her.

🔒 Spoiler

Hidden Heritage:
Farin is secretly half-demon—a fact even she does not yet realize. Her prophetic eye stems from a latent demonic trait: members of the demon race can briefly glimpse possible futures, the same ability behind the omens they once revealed to humankind.

Truth of her Vision:
Farin initial attempt on the Self-Divining ritual show a vision of the end of the world, where a future Villain is able to ascend to godhood, and it is the Villain who diffuse Farin vision.

View on the Winterlands:
Raised in the Springlands under heavy Church propaganda, Farin harbors ingrained cynicism toward the Winterlands people. Though not openly hostile, her distrust surfaces as cold sarcasm and passive-aggressive remarks. She sees their ways as crude, chaotic, and instinct-driven—everything her structured worldview resents. Over time, she may come to challenge these assumptions, but only through deep personal growth and lived experience.

Faith in the Goddess:
Farin still believes in the Goddess—not as a comforting presence, but as a distant, watching force. Though the Church betrayed her, she clings to the idea that her suffering must have meaning. Her worldview of "right" and "wrong" choices coexists with this faith by viewing the Goddess as the one who created the maze, while Farin must choose the path. She does not expect miracles—only that someone, somewhere, is still listening.

0.description:
You project your soul outside your body and weave it into a barrier to protect the targets from attacks.

Until this spell ends, each target may treat their Defense as being equal to 12 against any effects that target it
(they are still free to use their normal Defense score if higher than 12).

1.description:
You glimpse briefly into the future.

Until this spell ends, after a creature you can see performs a Check, if it was not a fumble nor a critical success, you may force that creature to reroll both dice.

Once you have forced two rerolls this way, this spell ends.

2.description:
You imbue a weapon with dark energy.

Until this spell ends, all damage dealt by the weapon becomes of the dark type.

If you have that weapon equipped while you cast this spell, you may perform a free attack with it as part of the same action.

This spell can only be cast on a weapon equipped by a willing creature.

props.notes_text:
Farin Fatuus (16)

【Apprentice Astrologian】

Character Notes

Standard Attire

Star-Blessed Orphan
Raised in a monastery orphanage; her unique eyes granted crystal-clear visions of future events.

Farin used this gift to win children’s games and help the locals with their problems, earning praise from the villagers.

Hunted Down
One night she revealed the secret of her predictions to a close friend, who then reported her to the Church Inquisition.

Suspecting a link to the long-defeated demon race, the Inquisition came for her. Farin escaped with the aid of her farsight but lost her right eye during the flight.

Saved by Master Lyra
Forced to wander from town to town, on the brink of starvation she was rescued by the renowned astrologian Lyra, who had foreseen their meeting.

Intrigued by Lyra’s mastery of “ordinary” astrology, Farin asked to become her apprentice.

The Night of the Ritual
Farin learned of a rite that lets one glimpse one’s own future. Disobeying Lyra, she performed the Self-Prognosis with her remaining eye as the catalyst. She saw a hazy vision of the World Tree before the sight was severed, leaving her cursed and unable to use her left eye’s power.

Present Goal
Seeking an artifact rumored to break the curse, she set sail aboard the SS Anne, said to carry a relic that dispels sorcery-born afflictions.

❝

“If the gods truly wish us happy, they wouldn’t fear my knowing tomorrow…
So why did they blind me?”

1.passive_description:
During a conflict, if you have two or fewer vanguard cards in play, you can use an action to choose 1 card from your hand and place it face down as a vanguard card.
If you do, draw 1 card from your deck.

When you suffer damage, if you have one or more vanguard cards in play, you may reveal one of them and place it on top of your discard pile.
If you do and that card is a joker or its suit matches the type of the damage you suffered, you instead suffer no damage and regain an equal amount of Mind Points.

At the end of each conflict, if you have one or more vanguard cards in play, shuffle them back into your deck.

2.passive_description:
When you acquire this Quirk, describe the nature of your curse and tie it to one of the threats present in your world. Once this threat is resolved, you will finally have a chance to break free from the curse – describe how you expect this to happen.

Examples:
Weapons you wield often miss their mark; your mere presence instills a sense of dread;
Your magic has a tendency to trigger unintended results;
Creatures within arm’s reach of you feel sharp pain across their bodies.

When you are about to perform a Check, you may instead describe how your curse gets in the way and automatically roll a fumble (both dice are treated as if you had rolled a 1 on them).
If you do, you receive 2 Fabula Points instead of 1, and generate an opportunity as normal.

If you ever manage to break the curse, immediately gain a Heroic Skill of your choice
(you may even choose a Heroic Skill whose requirements you do not satisfy, unless they include a Skill you don’t have).
This includes choosing a Heroic Skill for a Class you do not have.

3.passive_description: Once before the next rest, after the target performs a Group Check as leader or performs a Check to examine someone or something, they may add a bonus of +4 to the Result of that Check.

0.description:
Before you perform an Accuracy Check, a Magic Check for an offensive spell, or a Check to advance or turn back a Clock, you may declare "double or nothing".

If you do and the Check triggers a critical success, double the damage dealt by that attack or spell or the filled or erased sections of that Clock, respectively.

However, any other kind of success becomes a failure instead.

1.description:
When you generate a critical success or a fumble, you may draw 1 card from your deck.
If you do, discard 1 card from your hand.

2.description:
You gain a deck, a hand, and a discard pile.

During a conflict, you may use an action and spend up to 【25】 Mind Points

If you do, resolve 1 card from your hand for every 5 MP spent this way (to a maximum of 5 cards; these cards form a set).

After you resolve the effect of the set, discard these cards and draw that many cards from your deck.

3.description:
At the end of your turn during a conflict, you may discard up to 【1】cards from your hand.

If you do, draw that many cards from your deck.

4.description:
After an enemy you can see performs an action during a conflict, you may declare one of your deck’s suits (after the action has been resolved) and put the first card on the bottom of your deck in your discard pile, face up.

If that card is a joker or its suit matches the one you declared, you may immediately perform the Spell action for free, casting a spell with a total Mind Point cost equal to or lower than 【20】 (you must still pay its MP cost).

5.description:
You have a lucky number; at the beginning of each session, that number is 7.

Once per scene, after you perform a Check, you may replace the value shown on one of the dice you rolled with your lucky number
(even if this would give an impossible Result, such as a value of 7 on a d6).

If you do, the replaced value becomes your new lucky number.

6.description:
Each time you acquire this Skill, learn one Entropist spell.

Offensive (⚡) Entropist spells use 【INS + WLP】 for the Magic Check.

7.description: Your Accuracy Checks with brawling, dagger, flail, and thrown weapons trigger a critical success if both dice show the same number (and the Check is not a fumble).

8.description:
Each time you acquire this Skill, learn one Spiritist spell.

Offensive (⚡) Spiritist spells use 【INS + WLP】 for the Magic Check.

props.zero_effect_description:
Reveal the top 4 cards of your deck. For each card revealed this way, choose an ally who has not been chosen by this effect yet. They receive one of the following effects (the same effect may be chosen again for another ally):

EffectDescription
Boost CheckGain a bonus on their next check equal to 【The value of the revealed card】.
Free AttackPerform a Free Attack, ignoring HR. This attack gains bonus damage equal to 【The value of the revealed card】, and its damage type becomes the same as 【the suit of the revealed card】.
Recover HPRecover HP equal to 【The value of the revealed card × 10】.
Recover MPRecover MP equal to 【The value of the revealed card × 10】.
ShieldGain a Shield equal to 【The value of the revealed card × 3】.
Extra TurnGain 1 turn activation. Can only be chosen if the revealed card is a Joker.

After resolving this effect, place all cards revealed this way into the Discard Pile.
props.zero_trigger_description:
Whenever Farin roll a Critical Sucess or Fumble that isn't trigger by the Cursed quirk, gain 1 zero power

If this is the first time this effect triggers in this scene, gain 3 instead.
